payload.setup: Strive is a bitcoin treasury company. Its shares closed at $25.635 on 15 October 2026 after a 107.7% three-month gain and are now cooling; the planned SATS preferred sale and the bitcoin price drive the common residual.
payload.economic_basis: Strive's main asset is 32,773 bitcoin after it bought 3,311 for about $280 million at roughly $84,500 each on 5-9 October 2026, and it plans to sell 5 million SATS preferred shares at $100 each for $500 million with a 15% dividend and ranking behind about 13% SATA preferred, so roughly $75 million a year is paid ahead of common. Common holders get only the residual after those claims, so more bitcoin helps per-share value only if bitcoin's return beats the financing cost and the new preferred does not take the gain; the bitcoin per diluted share, common share count and source of past purchase cash remain unknown.
evidence: On 15 October 2026 ASST closed at $25.635 after a 3.89% daily gain and a 107.7% three-month return; the screen tag was 'Up / cooling'.

Strive bought 3,311 bitcoin for about $280 million at an average $84,500 per coin from 5 to 9 October 2026, taking holdings to 32,773 bitcoin ([Benzinga](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62320971/strive-acquires-3-311-bitcoins-average-price-84-500-bitcoin-oct-5-through-oct-9)).

Strive announced a $500 million initial public offering of 5 million 15% Series A perpetual SATS preferred shares at $100 each, ranking behind the SATA preferred; the sale had not completed ([CoinDesk](https://coindesk.com/markets/2026/10/13/strive-to-ipo-second-preferred-share-class-as-it-looks-to-further-build-bitcoin-treasury)).

forecast.pricing_assessment: The $25.635 close comes after a 107.7% three-month gain, so the price likely includes a large bitcoin premium and a completed $500 million SATS sale; that is my estimate, not a measured market expectation. With no disclosed bitcoin-per-share value, the short depends on bitcoin holding near the $84,500 purchase price and the sale proceeds not lifting bitcoin per common share.
assumptions: Bitcoin stays near the $84,500 average purchase price or does not rise enough to cover the roughly $75 million annual preferred dividend by mid-January 2027.
The SATS sale closes without a disclosed rise in bitcoin per diluted common share, or proceeds are held rather than used to buy bitcoin or repurchase shares at a discount.
No large asset sale, new common issuance or buyback changes the common claim before 15 January 2027.
forecast.opposing_case: The SATS sale could add $500 million of bitcoin or buybacks at a premium and raise bitcoin per common share, while a bitcoin rally would make the preferred dividend look cheap. TD Cowen's $132,750 bitcoin view for 2028 and the 2x ASST fund could also pull buyers into the stock before January.

calls.hypothesis: Strive's common shares will trade lower by 15 January 2027 because the 15% SATS preferred and existing SATA preferred take cash before common holders while the 107.7% three-month gain cools. If bitcoin stays near the $84,500 purchase price and new money does not raise bitcoin per common share, the residual value per share falls.
calls.invalidation: A disclosed rise in bitcoin per diluted common share after the SATS sale, or a bitcoin gain on the 32,773 coins that exceeds the roughly $75 million annual preferred bill, would disprove the short.
tail_risks: Bitcoin rallies sharply, increasing the value of the 32,773 coins and making the preferred dividend small relative to gains.
Strive completes the SATS sale and immediately buys bitcoin or repurchases common shares, lifting bitcoin per share.
A 2x ASST fund attracts large inflows and amplifies a rally, forcing short covering.
evidence_limits: Find the current bitcoin per diluted common share and the common share count; this decides whether $25.635 is a premium or discount to the bitcoin claim.
Find the source of cash for the October bitcoin purchases and reconcile the weekly reports with the 7,773-coin increase; this shows whether past buying added debt or preferred claims.
Find the final SATS sale terms and the planned use of proceeds; this decides whether the $500 million adds bitcoin per common share or mainly serves preferred holders.
